Lina felt the shorter ladder would make the work slower. Her uncle agreed, then explained that speed was not the only condition for choosing a tool. They marked the damaged ladder and set it aside for repair. The adults used the sound shorter ladder and a long picking tool for the remaining branches. Lina helped sort the fruit on the ground.
At the end, a few high apples remained. Lina expected her uncle to be annoyed. Instead, he said they had finished the work they could do with suitable equipment that day. He would return after the repair, rather than turn an unfinished task into a reason to use an unsuitable ladder. Lina looked at the few apples differently: they marked a limit to respect, not a failure to hide.

originalGroup.material:
Repair Manual Model Number 021

The design club found an old lamp and a manual that looked as if it belonged to it. Both showed the same brand name. A pupil wanted to follow the manual to change a part. The teacher asked them to compare the model numbers first. The lamp was Model 24, while the manual was for Model 42.
The drawings looked similar, but the switch and cable position differed. The club stopped the repair plan and asked a qualified repairer to inspect the lamp. He found the correct instructions and explained which checks he needed to make. Pupils observed and wrote notes; they did not work on the electrical parts themselves. The wrong manual was labelled clearly and filed with its own model number, rather than left beside the lamp again. The club’s report said that a familiar brand and similar appearance were clues, not enough evidence that instructions matched.
